For the process γ (high-energy) + γ (CMB) → e⁺ e⁻ the invariant energy squared must at least equal the squared rest-mass energy of the electron–positron pair:

s ≥ (2mₑ)² = 4mₑ² .

For two photons,  
s = 2E₁E₂(1 − cosθ).

The most favorable (lowest-energy) configuration is a head-on collision (θ = π), giving  
(1 − cosθ) = 2 ⇒ s = 4E₁E₂.

Setting the threshold condition:

4E₁E₂ = 4mₑ²  ⇒  E₁E₂ = mₑ².

Take the CMB photon energy  
E₂ ≈ 10⁻³ eV.

Electron rest mass:  
mₑ = 0.511 MeV = 5.11 × 10⁵ eV,  
so  
mₑ² = (5.11 × 10⁵ eV)² ≈ 2.61 × 10¹¹ eV².

Therefore

E₁ = mₑ² / E₂  
   ≈ (2.61 × 10¹¹ eV²) / (10⁻³ eV)  
   ≈ 2.61 × 10¹⁴ eV  
   = 2.61 × 10⁵ GeV.

Thus γ-rays with energies above roughly 2.6 × 10⁵ GeV will readily annihilate with CMB photons, limiting their lifetimes in the universe.

Answer: B
